subject.title: refactor(plugin-sdk): isolate core session state from plugin mutations

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally break the released `getAcpSessionManager()` class-identity contract now, or require an additive facade and deprecation path while securing session reads and mutations?
rationale: The isolation goal is valid, but source inspection cannot decide whether the project accepts an immediate shipped Plugin SDK break or which current-main recovery representation is canonical.

options.title: Rebase and preserve compatibility
options.body: Protect the current-main recovery fields, add a safe facade API, and retain or deprecate the shipped getter until an approved breaking-release boundary.

options.title: Approve the breaking facade
options.body: Explicitly accept the class-identity break, document the upgrade impact, and require rebased compatibility and live proof before merge.

options.title: Pause the split series
options.body: Pause or close these stacked branches if the recovery model already on current `main` is the canonical direction and this alternate aggregate should not proceed.

recommendation.title: Rebase and preserve compatibility
recommendation.body: Protect the current-main recovery fields, add a safe facade API, and retain or deprecate the shipped getter until an approved breaking-release boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice governs a released Plugin SDK contract and the canonical core session-state model rather than a mechanical implementation detail.
